answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register each identity by burning cryptographic stake via a verifiable delay function at dawn. The burning cost scales superlinearly as C(n) = k * n^2 for n concurrent identities, imposing prohibitive economic friction. An attacker attempting to crack protocol consensus like a brittle walnut discovers costs outpace rewards, while every verified transaction is etched into the ledger as if signed by an immutable quill.
